rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Refining chemistry reshapes molecules to suit engines. **Cracking** breaks large hydrocarbons into smaller useful ones — thermally (~500–700 °C) or catalytically (zeolite, ~450–500 °C), e.g. **C₁₀H₂₂ → C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄** — supplying petrol-range alkanes and alkene feedstock. **Reforming** (Pt, ~500 °C) keeps the size and changes the shape: straight chains become branched alkanes and aromatics (n-hexane → benzene).…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Octane number measures the knock resistance of petrol on a scale of iso-octane = 100 to n-heptane = 0; cetane number measures the ignition quality of diesel on a scale of n-cetane = 100 to α-methylnaphthalene = 0."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***One molecule, two ratings*** — n-heptane is the zero of the octane scale but its straight-chain brother n-cetane is the 100 of the diesel scale: the same molecular shape that ruins petrol makes perfect diesel.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Making Petrol Behave Crude oil gives long-chain hydrocarbons; engines want branched ones. **Cracking** breaks big molecules into useful small ones, **reforming** reshapes straight chains into branched/aromatic ones, and the **octane number** measures the result. For diesel the logic reverses — the **cetane number** rewards straight chains.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Cracking - **Cracking:** decomposition of **large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, more useful ones** by heat, with or without a catalyst. - **Thermal cracking:** high temperature (~500–700 °C) and pressure.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Cracking = size down (C10H22 -> C8H18 + C2H4); reforming = shape change (Pt, 500 C). Octane: iso-octane 100 / n-heptane 0; cetane: n-cetane 100 / alpha-methylnaphthalene 0. Branched = octane up, cetane down.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: All three petrol technologies are the same idea in different clothes: create or preserve branching, because branched molecules burn smoothly and straight molecules knock.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Cracking: large hydrocarbons -> smaller useful ones by heat (~500-700 C thermal) or catalyst (catalytic: zeolite, ~450-500 C); C10H22 -> C8H18 + C2H4; gives petrol-range alkanes + alkenes feedstock. Reforming: straight-chain -> branched/aromatic same carbon number (Pt, ~500 C, platforming); n-hexane -> benzene + H2.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Modern pump petrol is typically 87–95 octane; the lead additive TEL that once supplied cheap octane is now banned everywhere because leaded exhaust poisoned a generation of children.

Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why branched fuels resist knocking - In a straight-chain alkane, compression and heat ignite the end gases **before the spark** — a pressure spike = knock. Branched molecules burn more slowly and uniformly, waiting for the flame front — high octane.…  ·  ## 5. rows.text: Explain why TEL was phased out and what replaced it.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Octane number is not the % of octane in the fuel:** it is the % of iso-octane in the *comparison mixture* that matches the fuel's knocking — a fuel's own octane content is irrelevant to the rating.  ·  **Cracking and reforming are not synonyms:** cracking cuts molecules apart; reforming rearranges them. Different chemistry, different catalysts, different products.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Higher cetane = easier ignition = good diesel; higher octane = harder ignition = good petrol:** the two scales reward opposite behaviour — never mix them up.  ·  ## 7.
